7.text: MAGIC MEDICINE. — The Chukchee, as said before, ascribe all maladies

8.text: to the influence of “genuine” keˊlet, the murderers.¹ Of these, the keˊlet of

9.text: contagious diseases — such as small-pox, influenza, and measles — are so

10.text: terrible that the shamans are almost powerless to check them. “Against

11.text: those it is no use to begin,” said Scratching-Woman to me naively, “lest they

12.text: grow angry and retaliate upon ourselves.”

13.text: Another Chukchee explained that even sacrifices are of little avail with

14.text: those keˊlet. The people on the western tundra on the Kolyma explained

15.text: to me that in the “bad year” (1884), the year of the small-pox epidemic,

16.text: some of the people tried to propitiate the keˊlᴇ with sacrifices. Because he

17.text: was killing people in the inner room, women sacrificed to him with oil from

18.text: the lamp and with warm blood-soup from the cooking-kettle. These they would

19.text: put on small round pieces of curried leather, and then set them on the snow

20.text: pointed to the west, whence the keˊlᴇ used to come. But he wanted more

21.text: than that, and did not relent in the least, even after receiving these offerings.

22.text: The sacrifice of something that is very personal, and highly valued by

23.text: the owner, — as the Chukchee say, “taken to the heart” (liˊñliñkin), — is

24.text: considered an effective means of warding off an assault by keˊlet. The best

25.text: reindeer-team, the gun, or the clothes from the body, may serve for the

26.text: purpose. If a man once loudly proclaims his readiness to give to the keˊlet

27.text: any such object, it is very dangerous for him to go back on his promise.

28.text: The keˊlet would be sure to avenge heavily their disappointment at the loss

30.text: In a similar manner, when a man has once proclaimed a desire to die,

31.text: be it from spite or rashness, he must fulfil it, otherwise his whole family will

32.text: be exterminated by revengeful keˊlet.³ Against the keˊlᴇ of contagious dis-

33.text: ease, however, all sacrifices of even the most valuable things are of no avail.

34.text: The only means of escape from the keˊlᴇ of contagious disease is by imme-

35.text: diate flight, in order to leave between the keˊlᴇ and the human people large
